mainTopic: Why משניות say "דרכים" or "דברים," and what the numbers in our משנה come to exclude
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why משניות sometimes say "דרכים" (ways) and sometimes say "דברים" (matters). First it says the אתרוג משנה uses "דרכים" to hint that an אתרוג grows like a vegetable. But the משניות about the כוי and about גיטין also say "דרכים," and nothing about their topics fits. So the גמרא gives one general rule: where a subject's laws split into different cases, the משנה says "דרכים"; where there is no split, it says "דברים." רבי אליעזר's wording, "like a tree in every matter," proves this rule. Next the גמרא asks what the numbers "three" and "two" in our משנה come to exclude. It answers that "three" rules out חופה. For רב הונא, who holds that חופה does work, "three" instead rules out חליפין. The גמרא begins explaining why: חליפין works even with less than a פרוטה, but a woman is not acquired for so little. That explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the אתרוג משנה says "ways"
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in ביכורים uses "דרכים" to hint that an אתרוג grows the way a vegetable does.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the משנה is teaching us that an אתרוג behaves like a vegetable. A vegetable needs all kinds of water, not just rain, and it is tithed according to when it is picked. An אתרוג is the same: it needs all kinds of water, and it is tithed according to when it is picked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the משנה in ביכורים, which says an אתרוג is like a tree in three "דרכים." It explains that the word "דרך" hints at the אתרוג's way of growing, which is like a vegetable's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא explained that our משנה says "דרכים" because of a man's "way" of seeking a wife. Then it asked why the אתרוג משנה also says "דרכים." The answer here also ties the word to the topic: an אתרוג's "way" is like a ירק, because it needs extra watering and its מעשר follows the time of picking.

keyTerms.meaning: Citron, the fruit used on סוכות
Vegetable
Picking or harvesting
Tithing, separating מעשר
This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: There, it teaches us this:
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה in ביכורים that says an אתרוג is like a tree in three ways.

phrases.english: that the way of an etrog is like a vegetable:

phrases.english: just as a vegetable's way is to grow on all water
phrases.notes: "All water" means it needs watering by hand too, not just rain.

phrases.english: and its tithing goes by the time it is picked,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אֶתְרוֹג דַּרְכּוֹ לִיגְדַּל עַל כׇּל מַיִם
phrases.english: so too an etrog's way is to grow on all water

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from just before this section about the ביכורים משנה's use of "דרכים."
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the word "דרך" to the special nature of the topic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ביכורים משנה says "דרכים" for no special reason, which would weaken the explanation given for our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: "דרכים" there hints that the אתרוג's way of growing is like a vegetable's.

steps.title: Challenge from the כוי משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about the כוי also says "דרכים," with no special "way" behind it, so it should have said "דברים."
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at the משנה we learned: a כוי has some ways in which it is like a wild animal, some ways in which it is like a domestic animal, some ways in which it is like both, and some ways in which it is like neither. It should have said "matters"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that "דרכים" is always tied to the topic. In the כוי משנה, there is no special "way" connected to the subject, yet it still says "דרכים."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanations so far tied the word "דרך" to something about the subject: a man seeking a wife, or how an אתרוג grows. The כוי is an animal whose status between חיה and בהמה is unclear, and nothing about it fits the word "way." So why not say "דברים"?

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose status is unclear: wild or domestic
Wild (non-domesticated) animal
Domestic animal
Let it teach, meaning "it should have said"
But what about what we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: But that which we learned in a mishna:
"A koy: it has ways in which it is like a wild animal,
and it has ways in which it is like a domestic animal,

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ דְּרָכִים שָׁוֶה לַחַיָּה וְלַבְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: and it has ways in which it is like both a wild and a domestic animal,
and it has ways in which it is not like
either a wild animal or a domestic animal."
Let it teach "matters"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the approach of step 1 by bringing a משנה where "דרכים" has no link to the subject.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that "דרכים" is used because of something special about the topic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כוי משנה uses "דרכים" even though nothing about the כוי fits the idea of a "way."

steps.title: Second challenge from גיטין
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in גיטין also says "דרכים" when comparing divorce documents to freedom documents for slaves, so it too should have said "דברים."
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, the משנה we learned says: "This is one of the ways in which divorce documents for women are like freedom documents for slaves." It should have said "matters"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second example of the same problem. The משנה in גיטין compares a גט to a שטר שחרור using "דרכים," with no special "way" behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This makes the challenge stronger. It now looks like משניות often say "דרכים" without any link to the subject, so the topic-based explanation does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore
Divorce documents for women
Documents that free slaves

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which we learned:
"This is one of the ways
in which divorce documents of women are equal to freedom documents of slaves,"
let it teach "matters"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second example to strengthen the challenge of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that "דרכים" is used because of something special about the topic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גיטין משנה also uses "דרכים" with no link to the subject, so the word cannot depend on the topic.

steps.title: New rule: a split into cases means "ways"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the topic-based approach. Where the subject splits into different cases (פלוגתא), the משנה says "דרכים"; where there is no split, it says "דברים."
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, wherever there is a distinction (the subject's laws split into different cases), the משנה says "ways," and wherever there is no distinction, it says "matters."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on linking the word to the topic and gives one general rule. The choice of word depends on whether the subject splits into different cases (פלוגתא), as with the כוי that is partly like a חיה and partly like a בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "אלא" tells us the earlier explanations are being set aside. The new rule works for every case: the word does not depend on the subject at all, only on whether the laws split into different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which drops the earlier approach
Literally a division. Here it means the subject's laws split into different cases.
Anywhere, wherever

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think step 1 still stands next to this rule. The "אלא" means the גמרא is replacing the topic-based explanations with this one general rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives us a general key for reading the wording of משניות all over ש"ס.

phrases.english: Rather, anywhere that there is a distinction
it teaches "ways,"
and anywhere that there is no distinction
it teaches "matters."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 2 and 3 by replacing the earlier explanations with a new rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New general principle replaces the earlier explanations
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "דרכים" is chosen because of something special about each topic.
steps.terutzMaskana: "דרכים" is used where the laws split into different cases (פלוגתא); "דברים" is used where there is no split.

steps.title: Proof from רבי אליעזר's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר, who says an אתרוג is like a tree in everything, uses the word "דבר." This supports the new rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording of the משנה fits this too, because the end of that משנה says: "רבי אליעזר says: an אתרוג is like a tree in every matter." Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the new rule from the end of the ביכורים משנה. רבי אליעזר holds there is no split at all, and he uses "דבר" instead of "דרך."
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion splits the אתרוג's laws, saying it is like a tree in some ways and like a vegetable in others, and it uses "דרכים." רבי אליעזר says it is like a tree in everything, with no split, and he uses "דבר." That is exactly the new rule, so the גמרא accepts it.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording also shows this
The last part of the משנה
Tree
Learn from it, meaning the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: The final rule: a משנה says "דרכים" where there is a פלוגתא or split, and "דברים" where there is none. The wording of רבי אליעזר proves it.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
for it teaches in the last part:
"Rabbi Eliezer says:
An etrog is equal to a tree in every matter."
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule of step 4 from the wording of a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that "דרכים" means there is a split and "דברים" means there is none
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר in the ביכורים משנה says "לכל דבר" when he gives no split.

steps.title: What do the numbers exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the numbers in our משנה, "three" and "two," and asks what each one comes to rule out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The number in the first part of the משנה comes to exclude what? The number in the last part comes to exclude what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It asks why our משנה gives exact numbers, and what other methods those numbers come to leave out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a משנה gives a number, it suggests there are no more than that many. So "three ways" to acquire a woman and "two ways" for her to acquire herself must be ruling something out. The next steps answer this, starting with step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: The number, the count given
The first part of the משנה
To exclude what?

phrases.english: The number in the first part comes to exclude what?
The number in the last part comes to exclude what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about the wording of our משנה, after the "דרכים" topic is closed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which methods of acquiring, and which methods of becoming free, the numbers "three" and "two" come to exclude

steps.title: The number three rules out a wedding canopy
steps.stepSummary: The number "three" in the first clause of the משנה comes to rule out חופה as a way of marrying a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: The number in the first part of the משנה is there to rule out חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. It says the word "three" in the first clause tells us that חופה is not one of the ways to marry a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה opens with "a woman is acquired in three ways" and then lists כסף, שטר, and ביאה. Since the list is spelled out, the count seems extra, so it must be teaching something. It teaches that there are only three, so חופה is not a fourth.

keyTerms.meaning: To rule out or exclude
Wedding canopy; the bride entering the groom's domain

phrases.english: The number in the first clause comes to exclude a wedding canopy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 for the first number, "three."
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "Three" excludes חופה as a way of making קידושין.

steps.title: According to רב הונא, what does the number rule out?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that חופה does make קידושין. So for him, the number "three" cannot be ruling out חופה. What does it rule out?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב הונא, who says חופה acquires a woman (learned by a קל וחומר), what does the number come to rule out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 7 using the opinion of רב הונא. For him, חופה works, so the number "three" needs a different purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer "it excludes חופה" only works for those who say חופה does not make קידושין. רב הונא learns from a קל וחומר that חופה does work. So for him the extra number is still unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Acquires; here, makes the קידושין take effect
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

phrases.aramaic: וּלְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר חוּפָּה קוֹנָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: And according to Rav Huna, who said a wedding canopy acquires by an a fortiori argument,
what does it come to exclude?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר חוּפָּה קוֹנָה מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר, לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7 from the opinion of רב הונא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רב הונא, חופה does make קידושין, so the number cannot exclude it. Its purpose is still unknown.

steps.title: For רב הונא, the number rules out symbolic exchange
steps.stepSummary: For רב הונא, the number rules out חליפין. We might have thought חליפין works for a woman, because marriage is learned from the field of עפרון, and a field can be acquired with חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to rule out חליפין. You might have thought: since we learn קיחה (taking) from קיחה used for the field of עפרון, then just as a field can be acquired with חליפין, a woman can also be acquired with חליפין. So the משנה teaches us that she cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, for רב הונא, "three" rules out חליפין. It also explains why we needed to be told this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין with money is learned from the word קיחה, which is also used when אברהם bought the field of עפרון. A field can be bought with חליפין, so we might copy that to a woman too. The number "three" blocks this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Symbolic exchange: acquiring something by handing over an object, such as a cloth, in return
It could have entered your mind; what we might have thought
"Taking"; the word linking marriage to buying a field
The field אברהם bought from עפרון
It teaches us (that this is not so)

phrases.english: To exclude symbolic exchange.
It might enter your mind to say,
since we learn "taking" from "taking" in the field of Ephron,
phrases.notes: "כי יקח איש אשה" (דברים 24:1) is linked to "נתתי כסף השדה קח ממני" (בראשית 23:13).

phrases.english: just as a field is acquired through symbolic exchange,
so too a woman is acquired through symbolic exchange,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8 by giving the number a new job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the number a different exclusion that fits רב הונא's opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the קיחה link to the field of עפרון, a woman could be acquired with חליפין just like a field.
steps.terutzMaskana: The number "three" teaches that חליפין does not make קידושין.

steps.title: Maybe symbolic exchange really does work for a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: maybe the comparison to a field is right, and a woman really can be acquired with חליפין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is so: a woman can be acquired with חליפין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions step 9. If the comparison to the field is so strong, why not accept it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 called the חליפין idea a mistake that the משנה corrects. Here the גמרא asks why it is a mistake at all. The גמרא then needs a reason that חליפין cannot work for a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (that...)
So; in this way
Also; indeed

phrases.english: But say that it is indeed so!
phrases.notes: He means: maybe a woman really can be acquired with חליפין, just like a field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 9's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the חליפין comparison is wrong
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The link between קיחה and קיחה seems to support חליפין for a woman, so why reject it?

steps.title: Symbolic exchange works with less than a פרוטה, but a woman does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer: חליפין works even with an item worth less than a פרוטה, but a woman is not acquired with less than a פרוטה. The sentence continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: חליפין works with an item worth less than a פרוטה, and a woman, with less than a פרוטה, [does not give herself over].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer to step 10. It points out that חליפין does not care about the value of the item, while a woman is not married with less than a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חליפין, even a tiny object of almost no value can make the deal. A woman will not let herself be married for less than a פרוטה. So חליפין cannot be a way to marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: They exist; they are effective
Less than the value of a פרוטה, the smallest coin that counts
The smallest coin of value in הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. The next words explain that a woman does not give herself over for less than a פרוטה.

phrases.english: Symbolic exchange works with less than the value of a peruta,
and a woman, with less than the value of a peruta,

steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a basic difference between חליפין and קידושין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the field comparison, חליפין might work for a woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: חליפין works with less than a פרוטה, and a woman cannot be acquired for so little, so חליפין is not a way to marry her.
